config.title: Write a function to flatten nested arrays

intro.title: Write a function to flatten nested arrays
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that takes a nested array (an array containing other arrays) and returns a new, single-level array with all the elements. You will learn the core programming concept of recursion, where a function calls itself to handle deeper levels of nesting. The main technologies involved are JavaScript functions, array methods like concat, and conditional logic. This exercise will help you understand how to process complex data structures step by step. By the end, you'll have a working flatten function that can handle arrays of any depth.
intro.usecase: Flattening nested arrays is essential when processing hierarchical data from APIs, such as user comments with nested replies or product categories with subcategories. Developers use this technique to transform complex nested structures into flat lists for rendering in UI components like comment threads, product filters, or dashboard widgets. For example, when displaying a multi-level navigation menu or processing form data with repeating sections, flattening arrays simplifies data manipulation and state management. This pattern also appears in data visualization tools where nested JSON needs to be converted to tabular formats for charts and tables.

objectives: Implement a function that accepts nested arrays as input
Construct a recursive algorithm to traverse multi-level arrays
Manipulate array elements to extract values from nested structures
Initialize an accumulator array to store flattened results
Apply conditional logic to differentiate between arrays and other data types
Integrate base and recursive cases to handle different nesting depths
Control the function's flow to process each element systematically
